title: Ohio's 12th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Ohio's 12th Congressional District pits incumbent Republican U.S. Representative Troy Balderson against Democratic challenger Jerrad Christian. The district covers a large swath of central and eastern Ohio, including Zanesville, Newark, and parts of Fairfield, Licking, Muskingum, Knox, Coshocton, Guernsey, Morgan, Perry, Delaware, Holmes, Tuscarawas, and Athens counties. Ohio redrew its congressional maps in October 2025, but the 12th District remains a reliably Republican seat rated as 'Solid R' by the Cook Political Report. Balderson, a three-generation auto dealer and former state legislator, is seeking his fifth full term, while Christian, a Navy veteran and software engineer, is running on a grassroots, people-first platform after winning a three-way Democratic primary.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the Ohio's 12th Congressional District general election as of June 2026. The district is rated 'Solid R' by the Cook Political Report.

candidates.name: Troy Balderson
candidates.summary: Troy Balderson is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 12th Congressional District, first elected in a 2018 special election. A lifelong Ohioan and former auto dealer, he serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and chairs the House Energy Action Team. He is a principled conservative focused on energy independence, rural health care access, and workforce development.

candidates.summary: Jerrad Christian is a U.S. Navy veteran and software engineer who grew up in poverty in Appalachian Ohio. He served as a flight deck fueler during Operation Iraqi Freedom and Operation Enduring Freedom before transitioning to a meteorologist and oceanographer role. He is running a grassroots campaign focused on universal healthcare, raising the minimum wage, public school funding reform, and reducing corporate influence in politics.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polls exist for this race as of June 2026, and non-polling signals are consistent. Troy Balderson is the five-term incumbent in a district that the Cook Political Report rates as 'Solid R' and that remained reliably Republican after the 2025 redistricting. The Democratic challenger, while a credible Navy veteran and grassroots candidate, faces severe structural headwinds in a district not competitive in recent cycles. Without any polling evidence, the forecast relies entirely on incumbency, district fundamentals, and expert ratings, which all point to a safe Republican hold. Confidence is medium due to the complete absence of polling data, but the underlying indicators are unusually consistent.
